1941

The fourth reunion was held at Savoy, Sunday, June 15, 1941. The meeting was called to order by President Lee A. Clark, who then turned the gavel over to Vice-President Edgar Anderson McMahon, with request to preside. Mrs. Martha Buford May served as secretary.

The principal address of the occasion was delivered by Harvey J. Davis of McKinney. There was a prayer for Savoy and the singing of a few songs with Miss Aileen McMahon at the piano. Honorable J. R. May, Jr., Mayor of Savoy, delivered an address of welcome, to which response was made by J. Bettis Brixey of Atoka, Oklahoma.

The principal address of the occasion was delivered by Major M. McMahon of Fort Worth (son of the president), which he closed by saying, "although there is much trouble in the world today, he still maintains his confidence in his country and faith in our fellow man."

The morning session closed with the singing of the College Reunion Song, and an intermission of two hours was had in which lunch and happy memories were shared in the shade of the old walnut trees.

Reports of committees were heard and acted upon in the afternoon session. The report of the Committee on Nominations was adopted without change, in which officers were elected as follows: President, Edgar Anderson McMahon; vice-presidents, John Marcus Gist, Lee A. Clark and Guy P. Webb; secretary-treasurer-post laureate, Mrs. Martha Buford May; historian-librarian, Mrs. Pamela Paxton Boyd; board of managers, J. B. DuJerrett, Gus W. Thomassen and Mrs. Beulah Thomassen Stinnett.

The secretary was instructed to send a message of condolence to Doctor and Mrs. W. B. DuJerrett because of the illness preventing their attendance; an invitation from the Sherman Chamber of Commerce to hold the next reunion in Sherman was received through Barlow Roberts, which was declined with thanks.
